question: Why does clumping keep only one SNP from each group of correlated SNPs?

answers.answer: SNPs in LD carry the same association signal, so including all of them would count it many times
answers.feedback: Right. Clumping keeps the most significant SNP (the index SNP) and drops the SNPs in LD with it.
LD is a real feature of the genome: nearby SNPs are inherited together.

answers.answer: Only one SNP per chromosome can be causal
answers.feedback: A chromosome can carry many causal variants; clumping removes redundancy within an LD region.

question: Which SNP becomes the first index SNP in clumping?

answers.answer: The most significant SNP (largest −log₁₀ P) that passes the threshold
answers.feedback: Right. Clumping works down the ranked list, starting with the strongest signal.

answers.answer: The SNP with the largest r² to its neighbours
answers.feedback: r² decides which SNPs join a clump; the index SNP is chosen by its P-value.

answers.answer: The SNP at the start of the chromosome
answers.feedback: Position does not decide; significance does.

question: In the LocusZoom-style plot, block 3 SNPs are significant but dark blue (r² < 0.2 with index SNP 7). What does clumping do with them?

answers.answer: They are not in SNP 7's clump; the most significant of them (SNP 13) becomes the next index SNP
answers.feedback: Right. Low LD with SNP 7 means they reflect a separate signal, so it gets its own index SNP.

answers.answer: They are dropped because SNP 7 is more significant
answers.feedback: Only SNPs in LD with an index SNP (r² above the threshold) are dropped with it.

answers.answer: All of them are added to the PRS
answers.feedback: Within block 3 the SNPs are correlated with each other, so only their index SNP is kept.

question: In the clumped simulated T2D GWAS, 26 index SNPs pass P < 5 × 10⁻⁸ and 59 pass P < 10⁻⁵. How many index SNPs are added by relaxing the threshold? (Press Enter after your answer.)

answers.feedback: Right. 59 − 26 = 33 extra index SNPs, a mix of real sub-threshold signals and chance peaks.
The 59 already include the 26 from the stricter threshold: 59 − 26.
The lenient set includes the strict set, so subtract: 59 − 26.

question: How is the P-value threshold for a clumping-and-thresholding PRS usually chosen?

answers.answer: Empirically: scores are built at several thresholds and compared in validation data
answers.feedback: Right. The best threshold differs between traits, so it is chosen from the data.

answers.answer: It is always the genome-wide threshold, 5 × 10⁻⁸
answers.feedback: Many of the best scores use far more lenient thresholds, which let in real signals just below genome-wide significance.

answers.answer: It is set by the PGS Catalog
answers.feedback: The catalog records scores; it does not set thresholds.
